summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly integrated AI/ML capabilities, with vector search becoming a critical infrastructure component—adoption grew 377% year over year, and by 2026 roughly 75% of enterprise AI applications are expected to depend on vector search for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and semantic search. Platforms now span from native vector-indexing engines to full in-database LLM inference, embedding generation, and model training, increasingly unifying operational data, analytics, and AI on single governed platforms. However, experts caution that vector databases are specialized similarity-search indexes and should not be treated as general-purpose data stores.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst) plus Snowflake Postgres for AI-ready operational data
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless, SQL-callable LLM functions (summarize, translate, sentiment, complete), fully managed embedding and vector functions, Cortex Search for hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. Snowflake Postgres unifies the popular operational database with Snowflake's analytics and AI on a single governed platform, and the Horizon Catalog adds governance across data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake offers built-in VECTOR data types, vector similarity functions, and managed Cortex Search service for vector/hybrid retrieval directly in the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated hosted LLMs (e.g. Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) callable via SQL and Python through Cortex functions; no external API plumbing required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex AI functions billed by tokens processed / compute credits on top of standard Snowflake warehouse and storage costs. No separate license, but LLM usage can add meaningful cost.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML for in-SQL model training/inference and Vertex AI integration for generative AI and remote model serving
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI for embeddings, generative text/multimodal models, and AI inferencing. BigQuery also supports Graph queries and hybrid search for building context-retrieval and RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides built-in vector embeddings storage, VECTOR_SEARCH functions, and vector indexes supporting vector, text, and hybrid search natively within the warehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Tight integration with Vertex AI / Gemini models via remote models (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) invoked from SQL for generative and embedding workloads.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go: BigQuery ML charges for bytes processed or dedicated slot capacity; Vertex AI model calls billed separately per Vertex pricing. Some built-in models priced differently from external/remote models.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database embedding generation and LLM calls
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector columns with exact and approximate (HNSW, IVFFlat) similarity search, while pgai enables embedding creation and LLM inference (e.g. calling OpenAI/Ollama) directly from SQL. This lets teams keep relational data and vectors together for RAG and semantic search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search requires the third-party pgvector extension; it is extremely popular and well-supported but is an add-on rather than a built-in engine feature.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai and related extensions that call external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) from SQL functions; depends on extension installation and external API access.
databases.pricing_notes: Core PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are free and open source; cost comes from self-hosted infrastructure or managed provider fees. No per-token database charge, but external LLM API usage is billed by the model provider.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend for inference
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications via standard SQL by invoking models hosted in SageMaker, Bedrock, or Amazon Comprehend directly from Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL queries. It is designed for low-latency inference against operational data without building separate pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not a native Aurora ML feature. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only through the third-party pgvector extension, which is separate from Aurora ML's SageMaker/Bedrock inference integration.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and Comprehend for text/generative and NLP inference invoked from SQL; also SageMaker-hosted custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Aurora ML charge for the integration itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/I-O costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend inference charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — create, train, and run ML models using SQL via Amazon SageMaker (incl. Autopilot) and Bedrock LLM integration
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data warehouse users to create and train models with the CREATE MODEL SQL command, leveraging SageMaker Autopilot under the hood, and run in-database predictions at scale. It also supports invoking Bedrock LLMs and remote models for generative tasks over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively part of Redshift ML. Redshift has added some vector/embedding support via Bedrock integration and the HNSW-based pgvector-like capabilities are limited; core Redshift ML focuses on model training/inference, not a built-in vector similarity engine comparable to BigQuery/Snowflake.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker models; supports generative AI functions and remote inference invoked from SQL within the warehouse.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML uses existing Redshift compute; training via SageMaker and inference via Bedrock/SageMaker are billed separately. Local model inference runs on Redshift nodes at no extra model charge beyond cluster cost.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI for model building/serving/fine-tuning and Databricks Vector Search for native retrieval
databases.description: Databricks offers Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing GenAI models and agents, alongside Databricks Vector Search, a managed vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables. The lakehouse unifies data engineering, analytics, and AI with Unity Catalog governance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, managed vector index that integrates with Delta tables and Unity Catalog for low-latency similarity and hybrid search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to hosted and custom LLMs (Llama, DBRX, external providers) plus fine-tuning, agent framework, and RAG tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, Model Serving, and Vector Search endpoints; billed on top of underlying cloud infrastructure. Foundation model and serving endpoints priced separately.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector indexing and search integrated with the document database
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and provides approximate nearest-neighbor (HNSW) similarity search plus hybrid/full-text search within the same Atlas cluster. It enables RAG and semantic search without moving data to a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in feature of MongoDB Atlas (via Atlas Search / $vectorSearch), indexing vectors directly in the document store with hybrid search support.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled proprietary LLM, but strong integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and other providers for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas managed tiers; vector search runs on cluster or dedicated Search Nodes billed by instance size and storage. No per-query license, cost scales with cluster/search node sizing.
